summary: Troopers report a late-night traffic stop on University Avenue in Fairbanks that ended with a man arrested inside an apartment building on Kathryn Avenue; no court case has been filed behind it. Fairbanks Police posted one arrest for Nov. 25, at the 1900 block of Airport Way. No new criminal case was opened at the Fairbanks court on Nov. 26, which is Thanksgiving, and none of the cases listed below moved. The 36 Fairbanks filings counted here are the weekly charges report's own count for its window of Nov. 19 to Nov. 25, and that report lists no cases at the Nenana, Healy or Delta Junction courts for the week. The report now lists 4FA-26-02345CR, filed Nov. 23, which the previous week's report left out.

entries.title: Failure to stop and resisting arrest: Daniel D. Bishop
body: Daniel D. Bishop, 54, of Fairbanks was arrested on charges troopers list as failure to stop at the direction of a peace officer, reckless driving, resisting arrest, driving while his license was revoked, and driving in violation of a license limitation. University Avenue near Goldizen Avenue, Fairbanks, Nov. 25 at about 10:11 p.m.; Alaska State Troopers.
Failure to stop at the direction of a peace officer means not pulling over when an officer signals. Resisting arrest means using force to resist being taken into custody.

Troopers say they tried to stop a pickup truck for an equipment violation, that the driver did not stop and kept driving, that he later stopped and tried to flee into an apartment building on Kathryn Avenue, and that he physically resisted being taken into custody. Troopers say alcohol and drugs were determined to be a factor and that the investigation is continuing.
He was remanded at the Fairbanks Correctional Center. Incident AK26116317. No court case has been filed.

entries.title: Indecent exposure and trespass arrest: Beattus Moses Jr.
body: Beattus Moses Jr., 64, was arrested on a charge of indecent exposure in the second degree with a victim aged 16 or older, and on a charge of criminal trespass in the second degree. Fairbanks Police recorded both as misdemeanors. 1900 block of Airport Way, Fairbanks, Nov. 25 at 3:00 a.m.; Fairbanks Police.

Indecent exposure in the second degree means exposing one's genitals with reckless disregard for the offense caused. Criminal trespass in the second degree means entering or remaining unlawfully on another person's premises.

Police case 26003573; court case 4FA-26-02343CR, before Judge Maria P. Bahr, with arraignment set for Dec. 1. The State has not yet filed a charging document in the case, and the court record carries no charge.
